clue.text: Crooked female of nursery rhyme

parts.note: crooked reads as 'carrying a shepherd's crook', the lost-sheep shepherdess of the rhyme, not dishonest

explanation.surface: A dishonest woman from a children's rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme shepherdess who lost her sheep is pictured holding a shepherd's crook.

clue.text: Homeless city female pleased to be settled in compartment

indicators.note: settled in tells us one word is lodged inside another word

parts.note: a bay is a compartment, as in a bomb bay or loading bay
glad means pleased

explanation.surface: A homeless woman happy to find a compartment to live in.
explanation.definitionFit: A destitute urban woman who carries her possessions in carrier bags is so called.

clue.text: Presumably he was spotted playing for children

definitions.text: Presumably he was spotted playing for children

parts.words: Presumably he was spotted playing for children
parts.note: spotted means wearing parti-coloured clothes, and playing a pipe he led the town's children away in the legend

explanation.surface: Someone was seen performing for kids.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary piper of Hamelin wore a multicoloured coat and lured away the town's children with his music.

clue.text: Possibly run and see to make certain

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged in another order

explanation.surface: Run over and check to be sure.
explanation.definitionFit: To make sure of something is to guarantee it.

clue.text: Do without a holiday abroad

parts.note: leave is time off, a holiday from work or service
out means away from home, abroad

explanation.surface: Going without a trip overseas this year.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to manage without it.

clue.text: Tender put up for capital statue

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: sore means tender, painful to touch

explanation.surface: An offer made for a statue in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' reads as an offer or bid; it is the adjective meaning painful. EROS is the famous winged statue at Piccadilly Circus in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged figure atop the Shaftesbury Memorial in Piccadilly Circus, London, is popularly called by the Greek love god's name.

clue.text: Vehicle needs protection at the front

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
a guard is a protection

explanation.surface: A vehicle needs a guard fitted at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading part of an advancing army or movement is its forefront.

clue.text: Love to have a role in pictures

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a part is a role in a play or film

explanation.surface: A sweetheart hoping for a part in the movies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pictures' looks like films, but it is the definition: a style of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical art is a style of abstract painting using visual illusions.

clue.text: An outside line to ring

parts.note: reads like a telephone call to an external number, but ring means circle and the line touches it from outside

explanation.surface: Asking for an outside line to make a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a straight line touching a circle at one point without crossing it has this name.

clue.text: Agrees to change gun ammunition

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of the word before it are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to swap the ammunition for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A grease gun is loaded with lubricant, so lubricant is that gun's ammunition.

clue.text: It plays without music

parts.note: plays means spouts water, as a jet of water plays, not performs music

explanation.surface: Something performs without any musical accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative water jet is said to play when it is running.

clue.text: Roman general with a hold on father

indicators.note: on means the next piece follows directly after the earlier ones

parts.note: a grip is a hold
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A Roman commander gets a grip on his dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa was Augustus's great general and admiral.

clue.text: The strength of the current?

parts.note: current suggests a river or sea, but it is electric current, measured in amps

explanation.surface: How strongly a stream is flowing.
explanation.definitionFit: The strength of an electric flow is measured in amps.

clue.text: Sort of bustle not immediately obvious

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to rearrange, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of bustle that goes unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delicate or understated is not readily apparent.

clue.text: It gives the retired member a warm feeling

definitions.text: It gives the retired member a warm feeling

parts.words: It gives the retired member a warm feeling
parts.note: retired means gone to bed and member means a foot, not a pensioned-off club member

explanation.surface: Something makes a pensioned-off club member feel content.
explanation.definitionFit: A woollen sock worn in bed keeps the feet warm at night.

clue.text: Pays out, but not in silence apparently

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the word before it are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone pays out money, though noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog that barks shrilly is clearly not quiet.

clue.text: Acknowledge the good work that hire-purchase companies do

definitions.meaning: to praise or recognise someone's efforts
finance firms let customers buy now and pay later on loan

explanation.definitionFit: Recognising merit and lending money on account share the same phrase.

clue.text: Abbot in a northern church has control

parts.note: Dom is a title given to a Benedictine abbot or monk
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An abbot in a northern church is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Supremacy or ascendancy over others is control.

clue.text: Purchase money always available on time

parts.note: L stands for the pound sterling, from Latin libra
ever means always
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Buying when money is always to hand on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like buying, but here it means a mechanical grip or advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanical advantage gained from a firm hold or lever is called purchase.

clue.text: Slug, say, represents danger to stray pets

indicators.note: re-presents, shown again in a new order, so the letters of danger are rearranged
stray means wandering about, so the letters of pets go astray

explanation.surface: A slug is a hazard to wandering pets.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is an example of a creature that damages cultivated plants.

clue.text: Material for European steel centre

parts.note: a German is a European

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of the five-letter word steel

explanation.surface: Fabric for a European steel town.
explanation.definitionFit: Material here means relevant, as in material evidence.

clue.text: Sign to appeal to males

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal or invocation, as in 'O Lord'
men are males

explanation.surface: A notice designed to attract men.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is a sign of things to come.

clue.text: Notice to keep out nothing in the accounts

definitions.meaning: no item recorded in a ledger

explanation.definitionFit: A prohibition sign and a blank ledger line share the same two-word phrase.

clue.text: Tax-protester who presented her buff form

definitions.text: Tax-protester who presented her buff form

parts.words: Tax-protester who presented her buff form
parts.note: buff means naked, not a tax form in buff paper; she rode naked through Coventry to protest her husband's taxes

explanation.surface: A tax protester submitted her beige tax return.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Coventry noblewoman rode through the streets unclothed to make her husband lift a heavy tax.

clue.text: Produced the rent

parts.note: rent reads as money for a landlord, but it is a tear in cloth, which was made by tearing

explanation.surface: A tenant came up with the money owed to the landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn cloth has a tear in it, so tearing made the split.

clue.text: Leader of a religious group?

parts.note: a flight of aircraft is led by an airman, and someone who flies is jokingly 'religious' as one who goes up to the heavens

explanation.surface: Who heads a church sect?
explanation.definitionFit: The one who steers and guides, whether a ship's guide or an aircraft's flier, leads the way.

clue.text: Surgeon upset about cold sponge

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around another
upset tells us the letters of surgeon are knocked into a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A surgeon is annoyed about a cold sponge used in surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponge' looks like a surgical swab, but it is a verb: to live off others. 'upset' rearranges SURGEON and 'about' puts it around C.
explanation.definitionFit: To cadge or freeload off others is to beg things without paying.

clue.text: One covering end of chin in spots

indicators.note: covering means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of chin

explanation.surface: Someone covering the tip of their chin because of spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition producing pimples.

clue.text: Flirting, having no head for marriage

indicators.note: having no head means the first letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: dalliance means flirting or amorous trifling

explanation.surface: Flirting with no thought of marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no head' removes D from DALLIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A union by marriage is an alliance, as between royal houses.

clue.text: The sound of a swan or seal

indicators.note: the sound of means the word is said aloud and a word sounding like it is written

parts.note: a cygnet is a young swan

explanation.surface: Wondering what noise a swan or a seal makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like the noise an animal makes; it is the homophone signal. A cygnet is a young swan, and a seal here is the kind pressed into wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet ring was used to stamp an impression in wax.

clue.text: Tips which are never mean

definitions.meaning: mean in the sense of average: the outermost values are never the average

explanation.definitionFit: The outermost points are never the middle average.

clue.text: Wisely arch about how old one is

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: arch means sly or knowingly roguish
your age is how old you are

explanation.surface: Being cunning about one's age, wisely.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with sagacity means acting judiciously.
